thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident P-864209 triggered for service inference-queue — High backlog / processing lag detected. Alert conditions: queue_depth > 10k, sustained enqueue rate spike, 95th latency jump. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/P-864209
ashley: acked on PD :white_check_mark: I'm on it, starting triage
kevin: I got the page too, standing by. Can someone confirm if autoscaler is spinning? last controller event ~5m ago according to logs
ashley: checking metrics now -> `sum(queue_depth) by (shard)` shows shard-3 with the majority of backlog. Prom query I'm using:
```
sum(queue_depth) by (shard)
```
mona: infra side: seeing node provisioning errors in cloud logs, lots of `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` for g5.xlarge in us-west-2 when trying to request 4 nodes
tristan: that would explain why HPA can't get new pods scheduled. scale-controller keeps requesting, cloud responds with capacity error so pods stay Pending
ashley: grabbing scale-controller logs:
```
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/scale-controller --since=15m | tail -n 200
# repeated: "Failed to create instance: InsufficientInstanceCapacity" and "attach volume timed out"
```
kevin: ops option: we can temporarily push workers into the reserved on-demand pool. I can create a nodegroup in reserved-pool and label for inference-burst. Will take ~3-4m to join
ashley: I can also run a manual scale to relieve pressure while we wait: `kubectl -n prod scale deploy/inference-worker --replicas=20` (was 6)
incident-bot: PagerDuty — Incident P-864209 acknowledged by ashley at 2026-03-15T19:04:22Z
ashley: manual scale issued. watching queue; rate of drain increased but still above normal. I'm also enabling temporary rate-limits for non-critical tenants to buy headroom: `ratelimit set --policy low-tier 10rps`
mona: opened cloud support ticket AWS-INC-9981 referencing the capacity errors and the manifest of requested instance types
tristan: also proposing fallback routing: send short/low-priority requests to cpu-fallback model to reduce GPU pressure. Rule: if backend_latency>500ms -> route to model=fallback-cpu-small
kevin: created reserved nodegroup (on-demand) and attached label `inference-burst=true` (change id c9f3b). New nodes are provisioning now
ashley: summary for customer-facing comms: "We are investigating delayed inference responses in us-west-2 affecting a subset of requests. We have initiated emergency manual scaling and limited lower-tier throughput to mitigate. Root cause appears to be cloud capacity constraints preventing autoscaler from provisioning GPU nodes. We'll update as we restore normal service." :email:
tristan: short tactical plan: 1) keep manual replicas until cloud confirms on-demand nodes healthy; 2) keep rate-limits in place until backlog < 500; 3) if backlog doesn't clear within 20m escalate to eng-sre for infra-level intervention; 4) create runbook note for spot->on-demand fallback
kevin: handing off to night oncall — chris, you're the responder for the next 30m. I'll add details to the PD incident and pin this thread. :rotating_light:
chris: acked handoff. reading notes. I'll monitor queue (1m windows) and escalate to eng-sre if backlog > 500 for two consecutive minutes. leaving PD note: "Monitoring; manual scaling and reserved nodegroup active."
incident-bot: PagerDuty — escalation scheduled: if chris does not acknowledge within 10m, auto-escalate to eng-sre
ashley: created a short runbook entry `oncall/inference/spot-fallback` with the exact manual steps and commands we ran (kubectl scale, temporary ratelimit, reserved nodegroup attach). Will expand for postmortem
chris: dropping nightly follow-up: will check cloud ticket status and whether autoscaler needs tuning (retry/backoff shorter, fallback to on-demand sooner). If we see repeated InsufficientInstanceCapacity errors we should add automatic fallback earlier in the scale window. :thumbsup:
